final_answer:
in a quiet valley lived a tortoise named tico, who spent his days crawling through sun-warmed dirt. one day, he watched a hawk glide effortlessly on the breeze and sighed, “if only i could fly.” he asked the wind, “why do you carry birds but not me?” the wind whispered, “because you do not ask what you are meant to do.”  

tico practiced for years—flapping his shell, leaping from rocks, and begging birds for lessons. a kind eagle offered wings, but tico refused, saying, “i want to fly my way.” he crafted paper wings and launched himself into the sky, only to crash into trees. time and again, he failed, yet he never gave up.  

one stormy night, tico climbed the tallest mountain. lightning split the sky, and he felt the wind’s fury. instead of fighting it, he curled into his shell and rolled downward. the wind lifted him, and he soared—not on wings, but with the wind’s will. he landed safely, realizing he had always been meant to move with the earth, not against it.  

moral: sometimes, the path to freedom is not in becoming what you are not, but in learning to move with what you are.
